agent_steps: Phase 3 logreg head → predicted intent + confidence for the message
Phase 4 FAISS index → top-K most similar historical evidence pairs
Phase 6 escalation policy → auto_handle / escalate (rule-based, explainable) — decided BEFORE any LLM call
auto_handle ⇒ Phase 5 grounded generation (six safety rules) → reply ready to send + heuristic scores
escalate ⇒ structured human handoff: reasons, top-3 evidence, optional acknowledgment template — no LLM call spent

policy.decision: escalate if ANY rule fires; auto_handle only when all rules pass
policy.safety_asymmetry: a false auto-handle is far costlier than a false escalation — the policy is deliberately conservative

rules.name: private_state_domain
rules.fires_when: predicted intent ∈ {account_icloud, billing_purchases, repair_warranty, security_privacy, support_process}
rules.why: the correct next step depends on private state the system cannot see (order, quote, account, identity, official channels); public generic advice risks harm
rules.provenance: Phase 2 taxonomy typically_escalated hints (4 of 5) + documented Phase 6 account_icloud refinement (decision log D25)

rules.name: unmatched_intent
rules.why: no groundable issue class; an evidence draft would rest on irrelevant historical cases

rules.name: sensitive_content
rules.why: payment/order language or private data (email, phone, card-like number) in the message must not be answered — or echoed — by a public auto-reply
rules.provenance: Phase 5 safety rule 4, applied at the decision layer as defense-in-depth against intent misclassification

rules.name: intent_confidence_gate
rules.why: Phase 3 measured 0.780 mean confidence on correct vs 0.508 on wrong test predictions; below the threshold the routing itself is unreliable
rules.provenance: INTENT_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD fixed since Phase 3 (.env, single source of truth)

rules.name: retrieval_evidence_gate
rules.why: Phase 4 measured Recall@5 0.826 above vs 0.586 below the threshold; weak evidence produces clarifying questions, which a human should own
rules.provenance: RETRIEVAL_THRESHOLD fixed since Phase 4 (.env, single source of truth)

consistency.description: the service's TypeScript policy mirror vs the Python policy applied to the same runtime signals (predicted intent, confidence, top-1 score) — must agree on every message

end_to_end_quality.note: fresh live decisions on rebuilt artifacts — may differ marginally from the Phase 6 offline evaluation if intent confidences / retrieval scores shifted across rebuilds; both runs are reported, neither is hidden

latency.note: escalations skip the LLM entirely — their end-to-end time is embedding + FAISS + policy only

auto_reply_quality.note: same transparent Phase 5 heuristics, computed by the service for the replies it did generate

honest_caveats: LLM outputs are nondeterministic: the auto-path replies and their scores describe the recorded run (see generated_at).
n=29 (golden test split); the end-to-end decision rates inherit the Phase 6 confidence-interval caveat.
Latency is measured on a shared sandbox VM and varies with load; relative auto-vs-escalate gap is the meaningful signal.
The consistency assertion checks the DECISION and rule ids; reason prose may differ in wording between implementations.

live_service.note: mini-services/retrieval-service (Bun + Python worker + z-ai LLM); the dashboard agent console calls it through the gateway via XTransformPort=3030
